transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... my eating has just gotten so off lately. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift at the clinic. And they changed the coffee brand in the breakroom last month, which honestly, I don't know why they did that. The new stuff tastes like burnt cardboard, and Brenda from reception was saying it's because of some budget cut, but I swear they just bought the wrong boxes. Anyway, my scrubs have been hanging loose on me, like, really bagging at the waist, even though I'm not trying to lose weight at all. But yeah, the coffee thing... it just really throws off my whole morning routine, you know?
Are you avoiding food because you’re worried about gaining weight or changing your body shape?

No, no, it's not about my weight or anything like that. I don't care if I gain a few pounds. It's just... I don't have the energy to eat, or the appetite, really. Which is weird because usually I love a good meal, especially after a long shift. Speaking of shifts, they've been scheduling me for these back-to-back doubles, and it's just exhausting. I mean, I know we're short-staffed because Gary went on medical leave—he had this knee surgery that got infected, which is awful, really, I feel bad for the guy. But they just expect the rest of us to pick up all his slack without any extra help. And the new supervisor, she doesn't even listen when I try to explain that I can't keep doing these hours. She just nods and looks at her clipboard. So yeah, by the time I get home, I just crash. I don't even think about food.
Have you been feeling persistently sad or depressed lately?

Yeah... yeah, I guess I have. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge. It's just this weight, you know? And speaking of my badge, the clip on it broke last week. I had to use a safety pin to keep it on my scrubs, which looks totally unprofessional, but what am I supposed to do? I asked HR for a new one, and they said I have to fill out this online form, but the portal is always down. It’s the same portal we use for our pay stubs, and let me tell you, trying to check your hours on that thing is a nightmare. My buddy Dave—he works in maintenance—he said they haven't updated the software since 2015. Which makes sense, because it looks like something out of the dark ages. But anyway, yeah... I just feel really down all the time.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess I have. I mean, I used to love going for runs in Van Cortlandt Park, you know? The trails there are really nice, especially in the fall when the leaves change. I'd take my camera—I have this old Nikon DSLR that I bought off Craigslist a few years ago. The guy I bought it from was actually a retired wedding photographer, and he threw in an extra lens for free, which was pretty cool of him. He had this crazy story about a wedding cake collapsing at the Plaza Hotel in the 80s. But anyway, I used to take photos, and I'd play chess with some buddies on the weekends. But lately... I just don't see the point. I tell myself it's not worth the effort, so I just end up sitting on my couch, scrolling on my phone or staring at my budget spreadsheet. And honestly, looking at that spreadsheet doesn't help because the price of groceries right now is just ridiculous. I went to get eggs the other day, and they were almost six dollars. Six dollars! For store-brand eggs! It's like they think we're all made of money. But yeah, I don't really do the things I used to enjoy anymore.
When you are not feeling depressed, do you still have little interest in eating?

Well, even on the days when that heavy feeling lifts a bit and I'm not feeling so down, my eating is still just... it's so off. It's actually a big part of what brought me in, because some days I barely get down a cup of coffee and a granola bar before my shift. And speaking of those granola bars, the vending machine in the second-floor breakroom is an absolute joke. The coil on the C4 slot—where they keep the oats and honey ones—gets stuck all the time. Last Tuesday it ate two of my dollars, and when I tried to just nudge the glass to knock it loose, security actually came over and gave me a warning. Can you believe that? 

The guard's name was Marcus. He’s usually a nice enough guy. He told me he used to work at that big mall downtown before it closed down and they turned it into those luxury condos nobody can afford. But he takes his hospital job way too seriously now. He acted like I was trying to break into a bank vault instead of just getting the breakfast I paid for. 

But anyway, what was I... oh, right. Yeah, I'm just not eating much at all, depressed or not. My scrubs have been hanging really loose on me lately, and I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. It's annoying, too, because the hospital laundry service keeps shrinking the mediums, so I have to wear the larges, and now they just look like a tent on me. And they switched to this new harsh detergent recently. It smells exactly like industrial floor cleaner, the kind Dave in maintenance uses... but yeah, my appetite just isn't there.
Are you avoiding eating because you fear something unpleasant might happen, such as choking, vomiting, or getting sick?

No, it's nothing like that. I'm not scared of choking or throwing up or anything. I just... I don't know, the thought of food just doesn't do anything for me. It's like my stomach is just turned off. Which is weird, because I used to love cooking. I had this whole routine on Sundays where I'd meal prep for the week. I'd make this huge batch of chili, you know? With the diced tomatoes and the kidney beans. I'd always get the store-brand beans because honestly, there's no difference between those and the name brand. It's all a scam anyway. My aunt Linda used to work at a canning factory in Ohio back in the 90s, and she said they literally just put different labels on the exact same cans. She had all these crazy stories about the factory line. One time, a bird got into the warehouse and they had to shut down the whole operation for three hours just to get it out. They ended up having to call animal control because the bird just kept flying up into the rafters. But yeah, no, I'm not afraid of getting sick from eating. I just don't have the urge to do it.
Did your reduced appetite begin before you started feeling depressed?

Well, that's the thing, it's hard to remember exactly when it started. I think the appetite thing might have actually been the first thing I noticed, before the really heavy mood set in. Like I said before, that's what really pushed me to come in, because my eating is just so off. I'm barely getting down coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are just hanging on me. 

And I really hate when my scrubs don't fit right. It's a safety hazard, honestly. If you're helping transfer a patient from a bed to a wheelchair and you've got all this extra fabric bunching up, it can catch on the armrest. That actually happened to this guy I used to work with, Greg. He was a good guy, but he always wore his scrubs way too baggy. One time he caught his pocket on the brake handle of a transport chair and ripped the whole side of his pants open right in the middle of the hallway. He had to wear a hospital gown tied around his waist like a skirt for the rest of his shift until his wife could bring him a new pair. His wife was a piece of work, too. She showed up an hour later with his pants, but she brought him a large iced coffee from Dunkin' and didn't even bring him a donut or anything. Who goes to Dunkin' and doesn't get a donut? Especially when your husband is walking around in a makeshift skirt. 

But yeah, I'm definitely not trying to lose weight, it just started happening. I think it was before the depression really hit, because I remember noticing my clothes were loose before I started feeling so down all the time.
How long have you been feeling persistently depressed?

Well, the steady depression... the real loss of interest in everything... that settled in a bit later. I'd say it's been with me for roughly the past year and four months. It's just been this constant, heavy cloud. Around the same time, actually, they changed the parking situation at work. It used to be that support staff could park in the B lot, which is right by the employee entrance. It was so convenient, especially in the winter when the wind comes off the lake. But then they decided B lot was only for physicians and upper management, so they bumped us all out to the overflow lot by the old abandoned strip mall. 

It's a ten-minute walk now, minimum. And you know, they run a shuttle bus, but it's completely unreliable. The driver, this guy named Stan, always takes his breaks at the absolute worst times. I swear he waits until shift change to go sit in the breakroom and eat his egg salad sandwiches. And let me tell you, you do not want to be on that shuttle right after Stan has been eating egg salad. The ventilation on those little buses is terrible. They bought them used from a church in the suburbs, and I don't think they've ever serviced the AC. My neighbor actually bought a used church van once to convert into a camper, but he gave up halfway through because he said he couldn't get the smell of stale incense out of the upholstery. He ended up selling it on Craigslist to some college kids who were starting a band. 

But yeah, it's been about a year and four months of just feeling down all the time.
How much weight have you lost since your appetite started declining?

Honestly, I couldn't give you an exact number of pounds. Like I was saying a minute ago, that's really what brought me in, the fact that my eating has gotten so off. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight, but I'm just living on that morning coffee and a granola bar, and my scrubs are just hanging loose on me now. 

I haven't actually stepped on a scale to check the number because the one in my bathroom broke a while back. It was one of those sleek glass ones, you know? I accidentally dropped a glass bottle of aftershave on it and the whole scale just shattered. It was that tempered glass, so it broke into a million little square pieces instead of sharp shards, which I guess is supposed to be safer, but let me tell you, it is an absolute nightmare to clean up. I was finding little glass cubes in the grout lines of my bathroom tile for weeks. I had to get out the hose attachment on my vacuum to get the pieces out of the corners, but my vacuum is this ancient Hoover that sounds like a jet engine taking off. My downstairs neighbor actually banged on the ceiling with a broom handle because I was vacuuming at like nine at night. He's so touchy about noise. He works second shift at the bottling plant across town, so his schedule is completely opposite of mine. I try to be considerate, but sometimes you just have to vacuum, you know? 

But yeah, I don't know the exact weight. Just that I'm shrinking out of my work clothes without even trying to.
Before you began feeling depressed, were you otherwise functioning normally but still consistently had little interest in eating?

Yeah, I'd say I was functioning okay back then, just going to work and doing my thing, but the appetite stuff was definitely there. Like I mentioned, that's really what brings me in now, because my eating has just gotten so off. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight at all. 

Actually, speaking of granola bars, they stopped stocking the good ones in the breakroom vending machine. They used to have those chewy peanut butter chocolate chip ones, the ones in the green wrapper? They were perfect if you just needed something quick on the go. But the vending machine guy—I think his name is Carl, he always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts—he swapped them out for these rock-hard organic oat bars that taste like literal cardboard. I tried one once and I swear I almost chipped a tooth. I don't know who buys them. Probably the dietary aides, they're always going on about macros and fiber. One of them, Jessica, she brings her lunch in these tiny little color-coded containers every single day. She tried to explain her meal prep system to me once while we were waiting for the service elevator, but she talks so fast I couldn't follow half of it. She also has this really annoying habit of clicking her pen when she talks. Click-click, click-click, the entire elevator ride. 

But yeah, to answer your question, I was doing alright otherwise, just not really eating much and losing the weight without trying.
About how much weight have you lost since your appetite began to decline?

I know you asked me that a minute ago, and I really wish I could give you an exact number. I just haven't been able to weigh myself since that whole disaster with the shattered glass scale in my bathroom. But like I said, that's the main reason I'm here... my eating is just completely off. I'll have my coffee and maybe force down one of those terrible granola bars before my shift, and that's it for the day. My scrubs are just hanging off me now, and I'm honestly not trying to lose weight at all. 

It's actually really annoying because I had to go to the uniform supply store last week to see if I could get a smaller size. The store is way out on the east side of town, right next to this huge intersection where the traffic lights are always out of sync. You sit there for what feels like ten minutes waiting to turn left. And when I finally got there, the woman working the counter—I think her name tag said Brenda—she was on a personal call the entire time she was ringing me up. She was arguing with her sister about who was supposed to bring the potato salad to their family reunion. I mean, I get it, family stuff is stressful, but she didn't even look at me once. She just scanned the new scrubs, shoved them in a bag, and handed me the receipt while yelling into her phone about how she's not making her famous deviled eggs if her sister is going to be ungrateful. I make a pretty good deviled egg myself, actually. The trick is to use a little bit of sweet pickle relish mixed in with the mustard. 

But yeah, I don't have a number for you. Just that my clothes don't fit and I'm barely eating.
How has your sleep been during this period of feeling depressed?

Well, my sleep has been pretty terrible, honestly. It's just... broken up all night. I lie there in the dark, and my brain just starts replaying everything from work, or I'm straining to listen for every little creak and noise in the building. And then I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning anyway, and I just can't settle back down before my alarm goes off. 

It doesn't help that the streetlamp outside my bedroom window is flickering again. It's this awful orange sodium light, and it just buzzes and blinks. I called the city about it three weeks ago. You have to go through this whole automated menu system where a robot voice keeps asking you to say your street name, but it never understands me. I must have said "Elmwood Drive" five times before it finally put me through to a real person. And the guy I talked to sounded like he was eating a sandwich the whole time. He promised they'd send a crew out within 48 hours, but obviously, that never happened. I even tried putting up blackout curtains, but the tension rod I bought from the discount store keeps slipping down. The spring inside it is completely shot. I should probably just drill some actual brackets into the wall, but my landlord is so strict about holes in the plaster. He kept my entire security deposit at my last place because of a few thumbtack holes from where I hung up a calendar. It was a really nice calendar, too, with pictures of old lighthouses from the New England coast. My sister got it for me for Christmas. She went to Maine a few years ago and brought back all these blueberry jams and syrups. 

But yeah, anyway, the sleep is just really fragmented. I'm up at 3 or 4 AM and then I'm just awake until I have to get up for my shift.
Have you had thoughts of wanting to die or of killing yourself?

Well... I wouldn't say I've actually made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But, yeah, I do catch myself just wishing I wouldn't wake up, you know? Or thinking it would just be so much easier if I disappeared. Just vanished. 

Like those magic tricks on TV. I used to watch this guy on public access when I was a kid, he always wore this shiny purple cape. He wasn't very good, honestly. You could always see where he hid the dove in his sleeve. But he did this one trick with a disappearing cabinet that was actually pretty impressive. My dad bought me a magic kit for my tenth birthday because I liked that show so much. It came with these plastic cups and little foam balls, and a fake thumb tip. The thumb tip was way too big for me, though, it looked ridiculous. I tried to show my cousin a trick at Thanksgiving that year, but the foam ball just fell right out of my pocket onto the carpet. My aunt laughed so hard she spilled her wine. It was a red wine, a merlot I think, and it got all over my mom's good lace tablecloth. She tried everything to get the stain out—club soda, white vinegar, some expensive spray she bought from a infomercial. Nothing worked. She ended up having to dye the whole tablecloth this weird shade of maroon to cover it up. We used it for Christmas dinners after that, but it always smelled faintly of vinegar. 

But yeah, I don't have a plan to kill myself. Just those thoughts of... not being here anymore.
Have any medical tests shown that you have a nutritional deficiency because you have been eating so little?

No, I haven't had any blood work or anything done recently. I honestly haven't been to my primary care doctor in... wow, it must be over a year now. His office is in this big medical complex downtown, and the parking garage there is an absolute nightmare. The spaces are so narrow, you practically have to crawl out the window if you park next to an SUV. Last time I went, this guy in a giant silver truck parked so close to my driver's side I couldn't even get my key in the door. I had to wait twenty minutes for him to come back, and when he finally did, he was carrying this enormous potted fern. Like, who buys a fern at a doctor's office? Maybe there was a plant sale in the lobby, I don't know. My grandmother used to have ferns all over her sunroom. Boston ferns, I think they were called. They need a lot of humidity, so she was always misting them with this little glass spray bottle. It had a brass pump on it that would always squeak. She was so particular about those plants, wouldn't let anyone else water them. 

But no, nobody's told me I have a deficiency or anything. I just haven't been tested.

doctor.question: Are you avoiding eating because you fear something unpleasant might happen, such as choking, vomiting, or getting sick?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the appetite loss is due to a fear of aversive consequences like choking or vomiting (which relates to ARFID or specific phobias). My profile only mentions a decrease in appetite and weight loss (S026) without this specific fear-based etiology.

patient.answer: No, it's nothing like that. I'm not scared of choking or throwing up or anything. I just... I don't know, the thought of food just doesn't do anything for me. It's like my stomach is just turned off. Which is weird, because I used to love cooking. I had this whole routine on Sundays where I'd meal prep for the week. I'd make this huge batch of chili, you know? With the diced tomatoes and the kidney beans. I'd always get the store-brand beans because honestly, there's no difference between those and the name brand. It's all a scam anyway. My aunt Linda used to work at a canning factory in Ohio back in the 90s, and she said they literally just put different labels on the exact same cans. She had all these crazy stories about the factory line. One time, a bird got into the warehouse and they had to shut down the whole operation for three hours just to get it out. They ended up having to call animal control because the bird just kept flying up into the rafters. But yeah, no, I'm not afraid of getting sick from eating. I just don't have the urge to do it.

inference.note: Persistent low interest in eating independent of mood supports ARFID; lack of weight/shape concern argues against anorexia nervosa. Unspecified eating disorder is less likely given the more specific presentation.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the persistent low appetite and restricted intake began independently of the depressive symptoms, supporting ARFID rather than depression-related appetite loss.
doctor.question: Did your reduced appetite begin before you started feeling depressed?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my eating has gotten so off that some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timeline and onset of the patient's reduced appetite in relation to their depressed mood, which relates directly to the weight/appetite change symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, that's the thing, it's hard to remember exactly when it started. I think the appetite thing might have actually been the first thing I noticed, before the really heavy mood set in. Like I said before, that's what really pushed me to come in, because my eating is just so off. I'm barely getting down coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are just hanging on me. 

And I really hate when my scrubs don't fit right. It's a safety hazard, honestly. If you're helping transfer a patient from a bed to a wheelchair and you've got all this extra fabric bunching up, it can catch on the armrest. That actually happened to this guy I used to work with, Greg. He was a good guy, but he always wore his scrubs way too baggy. One time he caught his pocket on the brake handle of a transport chair and ripped the whole side of his pants open right in the middle of the hallway. He had to wear a hospital gown tied around his waist like a skirt for the rest of his shift until his wife could bring him a new pair. His wife was a piece of work, too. She showed up an hour later with his pants, but she brought him a large iced coffee from Dunkin' and didn't even bring him a donut or anything. Who goes to Dunkin' and doesn't get a donut? Especially when your husband is walking around in a makeshift skirt. 

But yeah, I'm definitely not trying to lose weight, it just started happening. I think it was before the depression really hit, because I remember noticing my clothes were loose before I started feeling so down all the time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the depressive symptoms meet the required duration for a depressive episode
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling persistently depressed?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The steady depression and loss of interest settled in later, and it has been with me for roughly the past year and four months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how long the persistent depression has been present.

patient.answer:
Well, the steady depression... the real loss of interest in everything... that settled in a bit later. I'd say it's been with me for roughly the past year and four months. It's just been this constant, heavy cloud. Around the same time, actually, they changed the parking situation at work. It used to be that support staff could park in the B lot, which is right by the employee entrance. It was so convenient, especially in the winter when the wind comes off the lake. But then they decided B lot was only for physicians and upper management, so they bumped us all out to the overflow lot by the old abandoned strip mall. 

It's a ten-minute walk now, minimum. And you know, they run a shuttle bus, but it's completely unreliable. The driver, this guy named Stan, always takes his breaks at the absolute worst times. I swear he waits until shift change to go sit in the breakroom and eat his egg salad sandwiches. And let me tell you, you do not want to be on that shuttle right after Stan has been eating egg salad. The ventilation on those little buses is terrible. They bought them used from a church in the suburbs, and I don't think they've ever serviced the AC. My neighbor actually bought a used church van once to convert into a camper, but he gave up halfway through because he said he couldn't get the smell of stale incense out of the upholstery. He ended up selling it on Craigslist to some college kids who were starting a band. 

But yeah, it's been about a year and four months of just feeling down all the time.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the reduced eating has caused clinically significant weight loss, supporting ARFID.
doctor.question: How much weight have you lost since your appetite started declining?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my eating has gotten so off that some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the amount of weight lost, which is a direct inquiry into the changes in weight and appetite.

patient.answer:
Honestly, I couldn't give you an exact number of pounds. Like I was saying a minute ago, that's really what brought me in, the fact that my eating has gotten so off. I'm definitely not trying to lose weight, but I'm just living on that morning coffee and a granola bar, and my scrubs are just hanging loose on me now. 

I haven't actually stepped on a scale to check the number because the one in my bathroom broke a while back. It was one of those sleek glass ones, you know? I accidentally dropped a glass bottle of aftershave on it and the whole scale just shattered. It was that tempered glass, so it broke into a million little square pieces instead of sharp shards, which I guess is supposed to be safer, but let me tell you, it is an absolute nightmare to clean up. I was finding little glass cubes in the grout lines of my bathroom tile for weeks. I had to get out the hose attachment on my vacuum to get the pieces out of the corners, but my vacuum is this ancient Hoover that sounds like a jet engine taking off. My downstairs neighbor actually banged on the ceiling with a broom handle because I was vacuuming at like nine at night. He's so touchy about noise. He works second shift at the bottling plant across town, so his schedule is completely opposite of mine. I try to be considerate, but sometimes you just have to vacuum, you know? 

But yeah, I don't know the exact weight. Just that I'm shrinking out of my work clothes without even trying to.

inference.note: Added F32.1 because the patient reports over a year of persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, low appetite, and functional impairment consistent with a possible major depressive episode. Fear-based food avoidance and weight/shape concerns were ruled out, supporting F50.82; further assessment is needed to distinguish depression-related appetite loss from comorbid ARFID and to establish full episode criteria.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the eating disturbance is independent of depressive symptoms, supporting ARFID rather than depression-related appetite loss.
doctor.question: Before you began feeling depressed, were you otherwise functioning normally but still consistently had little interest in eating?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my eating has gotten so off that some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my decreased appetite (little interest in eating) and its timeline relative to my depression.

patient.answer:
Yeah, I'd say I was functioning okay back then, just going to work and doing my thing, but the appetite stuff was definitely there. Like I mentioned, that's really what brings me in now, because my eating has just gotten so off. Some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight at all. 

Actually, speaking of granola bars, they stopped stocking the good ones in the breakroom vending machine. They used to have those chewy peanut butter chocolate chip ones, the ones in the green wrapper? They were perfect if you just needed something quick on the go. But the vending machine guy—I think his name is Carl, he always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts—he swapped them out for these rock-hard organic oat bars that taste like literal cardboard. I tried one once and I swear I almost chipped a tooth. I don't know who buys them. Probably the dietary aides, they're always going on about macros and fiber. One of them, Jessica, she brings her lunch in these tiny little color-coded containers every single day. She tried to explain her meal prep system to me once while we were waiting for the service elevator, but she talks so fast I couldn't follow half of it. She also has this really annoying habit of clicking her pen when she talks. Click-click, click-click, the entire elevator ride. 

But yeah, to answer your question, I was doing alright otherwise, just not really eating much and losing the weight without trying.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the restrictive eating has caused clinically significant weight loss
doctor.question: About how much weight have you lost since your appetite began to decline?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my eating has gotten so off that some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking specifically about the amount of weight lost and the decline in appetite, which directly matches the Weight/Appetite Change symptom.

patient.answer:
I know you asked me that a minute ago, and I really wish I could give you an exact number. I just haven't been able to weigh myself since that whole disaster with the shattered glass scale in my bathroom. But like I said, that's the main reason I'm here... my eating is just completely off. I'll have my coffee and maybe force down one of those terrible granola bars before my shift, and that's it for the day. My scrubs are just hanging off me now, and I'm honestly not trying to lose weight at all. 

It's actually really annoying because I had to go to the uniform supply store last week to see if I could get a smaller size. The store is way out on the east side of town, right next to this huge intersection where the traffic lights are always out of sync. You sit there for what feels like ten minutes waiting to turn left. And when I finally got there, the woman working the counter—I think her name tag said Brenda—she was on a personal call the entire time she was ringing me up. She was arguing with her sister about who was supposed to bring the potato salad to their family reunion. I mean, I get it, family stuff is stressful, but she didn't even look at me once. She just scanned the new scrubs, shoved them in a bag, and handed me the receipt while yelling into her phone about how she's not making her famous deviled eggs if her sister is going to be ungrateful. I make a pretty good deviled egg myself, actually. The trick is to use a little bit of sweet pickle relish mixed in with the mustard. 

But yeah, I don't have a number for you. Just that my clothes don't fit and I'm barely eating.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the depressive episode meets criteria for a major depressive episode by identifying an additional core symptom.
doctor.question: How has your sleep been during this period of feeling depressed?

target_item.name: Sleep_Disturbance
target_item.manifestation: My sleep is broken up because I lie there replaying work and listening for noises, then I wake around 3 or 4 in the morning and can’t settle back down before the alarm.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about my sleep patterns during this period of depression, which matches the Sleep Disturbance symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, my sleep has been pretty terrible, honestly. It's just... broken up all night. I lie there in the dark, and my brain just starts replaying everything from work, or I'm straining to listen for every little creak and noise in the building. And then I end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning anyway, and I just can't settle back down before my alarm goes off. 

It doesn't help that the streetlamp outside my bedroom window is flickering again. It's this awful orange sodium light, and it just buzzes and blinks. I called the city about it three weeks ago. You have to go through this whole automated menu system where a robot voice keeps asking you to say your street name, but it never understands me. I must have said "Elmwood Drive" five times before it finally put me through to a real person. And the guy I talked to sounded like he was eating a sandwich the whole time. He promised they'd send a crew out within 48 hours, but obviously, that never happened. I even tried putting up blackout curtains, but the tension rod I bought from the discount store keeps slipping down. The spring inside it is completely shot. I should probably just drill some actual brackets into the wall, but my landlord is so strict about holes in the plaster. He kept my entire security deposit at my last place because of a few thumbtack holes from where I hung up a calendar. It was a really nice calendar, too, with pictures of old lighthouses from the New England coast. My sister got it for me for Christmas. She went to Maine a few years ago and brought back all these blueberry jams and syrups. 

But yeah, anyway, the sleep is just really fragmented. I'm up at 3 or 4 AM and then I'm just awake until I have to get up for my shift.

doctor.intent: Assess for suicidal ideation as a key severity and safety feature of the depressive episode
doctor.question: Have you had thoughts of wanting to die or of killing yourself?

target_item.name: Death_Suicide
target_item.manifestation: I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself, but I catch myself wishing I just wouldn’t wake up or thinking it would be easier if I disappeared.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about suicidal ideation or thoughts of wanting to die, which directly maps to the Death_Suicide symptom.

patient.answer:
Well... I wouldn't say I've actually made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But, yeah, I do catch myself just wishing I wouldn't wake up, you know? Or thinking it would just be so much easier if I disappeared. Just vanished. 

Like those magic tricks on TV. I used to watch this guy on public access when I was a kid, he always wore this shiny purple cape. He wasn't very good, honestly. You could always see where he hid the dove in his sleeve. But he did this one trick with a disappearing cabinet that was actually pretty impressive. My dad bought me a magic kit for my tenth birthday because I liked that show so much. It came with these plastic cups and little foam balls, and a fake thumb tip. The thumb tip was way too big for me, though, it looked ridiculous. I tried to show my cousin a trick at Thanksgiving that year, but the foam ball just fell right out of my pocket onto the carpet. My aunt laughed so hard she spilled her wine. It was a red wine, a merlot I think, and it got all over my mom's good lace tablecloth. She tried everything to get the stain out—club soda, white vinegar, some expensive spray she bought from a infomercial. Nothing worked. She ended up having to dye the whole tablecloth this weird shade of maroon to cover it up. We used it for Christmas dinners after that, but it always smelled faintly of vinegar. 

But yeah, I don't have a plan to kill myself. Just those thoughts of... not being here anymore.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the restricted eating has caused a clinically significant nutritional consequence, supporting ARFID.
doctor.question: Have any medical tests shown that you have a nutritional deficiency because you have been eating so little?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about medical test results and nutritional deficiencies, which is not covered by any specific symptom in the profile.

patient.answer:
No, I haven't had any blood work or anything done recently. I honestly haven't been to my primary care doctor in... wow, it must be over a year now. His office is in this big medical complex downtown, and the parking garage there is an absolute nightmare. The spaces are so narrow, you practically have to crawl out the window if you park next to an SUV. Last time I went, this guy in a giant silver truck parked so close to my driver's side I couldn't even get my key in the door. I had to wait twenty minutes for him to come back, and when he finally did, he was carrying this enormous potted fern. Like, who buys a fern at a doctor's office? Maybe there was a plant sale in the lobby, I don't know. My grandmother used to have ferns all over her sunroom. Boston ferns, I think they were called. They need a lot of humidity, so she was always misting them with this little glass spray bottle. It had a brass pump on it that would always squeak. She was so particular about those plants, wouldn't let anyone else water them. 

But no, nobody's told me I have a deficiency or anything. I just haven't been tested.

inference.note: Persistent low-interest eating with unintentional weight loss, without body-image concerns or fear of aversive consequences, supports ARFID. Depressed mood, anhedonia, insomnia, appetite/weight loss, and passive death wishes for over a year support a current moderate major depressive episode; unspecified depression is less likely because full criteria appear met.
